chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from some of our companions, from Nasr ibn Qabus, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and an abandoned well and a lofty palace». He said: The Abandoned Well is the Silent Imam, and the Lofty Palace is the Speaking Imam.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ الصَّامِتُ: The Silent Imam, one who holds knowledge but does not speak publicly
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ النَّاطِقُ: The Speaking Imam, one who articulates and proclaims the truth
key_terms.الْبِئْرُ الْمُعَطَّلَةُ: The abandoned well, interpreted here as the Silent Imam
key_terms.الْقَصْرُ الْمُشِيدُ: The lofty/strongly built palace, interpreted here as the Speaking Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'abandoned well' and 'lofty palace' in Surah Al-Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this allegorical exegesis of Surah Al-Hajj 22:45, distinguishing between the Imam who guards esoteric knowledge in silence (the 'abandoned well') and the one who actively propagates it (the 'lofty palace'). This distinction reflects the Shia theological concept of the Imam's dual role as both the hidden repository of divine truth and the public authority guiding the community, particularly during periods of political constraint or occultation.
